scenes.dialogue: On twenty eighth October, a two-judge Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Honourable Justice Atul S Chandurkar ruled.
scenes.shown: On 28 October, a two-judge Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Honourable Justice Atul S. Chandurkar ruled.

scenes.dialogue: South Bihar Power Distribution Company's franchisee contract required three arbitrators. By consent, the Patna High Court appointed a sole arbitrator.
Later, by consent, a former Chief Justice of India took over. Before one year, plus six months by consent, ran out, the respondents asked the High Court for four more months.
The appellant objected: three arbitrators, the claimant's insolvency, and the High Court's power to extend time. The High Court rejected every one of them.
On the panel, the Court held: having consented twice, taken part, and filed a counter claim, the appellant waived its objection under Section Four. It came too late.
scenes.shown: On the panel, the Court held: having consented twice, taken part, and filed a counter claim, the appellant waived its objection under Section 4. It came too late.

scenes.dialogue: And insolvency was no bar. The moratorium stops recovery against the debtor, not the debtor's own claim, which, if it succeeds, only adds to its value.
But acting under Section Eleven, the High Court could not extend time. That role ends once the tribunal is formed. Only the court defined in Section Two can.
scenes.shown: But acting under Section 11, the High Court could not extend time. That role ends once the tribunal is formed. Only the court defined in Section 2 can.

scenes.dialogue: Since the Patna Commercial Court had already extended the mandate, the error made no difference. The appeals were dismissed, and the award must come within six weeks.
